attrs.evidence: The premise is false. Advanced composition is O(ε√k) — TIGHTER than the additive kε, which remains a valid upper bound — and zCDP, Rényi DP at fixed order, pure ε and approximate max-information all compose exactly additively. An additive ledger is therefore the right shape. The 'quadratic' in the literature is the TRANSFER condition (budget ≲ n² overfitting detections), a statement about holdout size, not a composition law.
attrs.prior_art: Dwork–Feldman–Hardt–Pitassi–Reingold–Roth 2015 (Thm 3 basic, Thm 4 advanced, Thm 15 max-information, Thm 25 transfer); Bun–Steinke 2016 (zCDP); Mironov 2017 (RDP).
attrs.statement: Differential privacy composes quadratically under advanced composition, so CB2's additivity is the wrong law.
attrs.supersedes: INV-R1 Q4, which named this as 'the single most likely place the cross-family claim is wrong'. It was wrong, but not for the stated reason — the reason was LED-REV.
